data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel will outperform the expert because a trained non-expert panel functions as a *committee of weak learners* where the checklist provides the weak learning algorithm. The expert, despite higher individual competence, is a single strong learner prone to overfitting the training distribution. The panel's reliability gain is genuine if and only if it demonstrates robustness to distribution shift *relative to the expert* within the same evaluation. The distinguishing evidence is the error pattern on out-of-distribution cases identified within the evaluation: if the panel maintains accuracy where the expert degrades, the gain is genuine; if both degrade equally, the panel was merely compliant with a distribution-matched checklist.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Both panel and expert are evaluated on in-distribution cases only, making distribution shift undetectable","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's training distribution is shown to be identical to the evaluation distribution, eliminating the overfitting advantage","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's checklist is shown to have been overfit to the same training data as the expert, making both equally fragile","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Out-of-distribution cases are identified but both systems perform identically on them, suggesting the gain is distribution-dependent","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's robustness is explained by its refusal to answer on OOD cases, not by correct answers, inflating accuracy metrics","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A single expert overfits a specific problem distribution through years of experience, developing heuristics that are locally optimal but globally fragile. The non-expert panel, guided by a general checklist, underfits any specific distribution but is more robust across the broad space. This follows the bias-variance tradeoff: the expert has low bias, high variance; the panel has higher bias, lower variance. For verifiable tasks with sufficient breadth, the panel's lower variance dominates. Genuine gain is identified by probing distribution shift within a single evaluation: cases that deviate from the expert's training niche reveal whether the panel's reliability is structural (genuine) or coincidental (matched to the same distribution).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
